description.p: FrameExtractor is a modern cross-platform video frame extractor with a clean dark UI. It supports local video files and can download and extract frames directly from YouTube URLs.

ul.li: Extract frames from local video files (MP4, MKV, AVI, MOV, and more)
Extract frames directly from YouTube URLs via yt-dlp
Adjustable FPS, output format (PNG, JPG, WebP, BMP), quality, and scale
Live frame count and size estimates before extraction
Frame preview with scrubber before committing to a full extraction
Batch extraction across multiple time ranges
Preset system to save and reuse extraction settings
Extraction history with one-click re-extraction

description.p: Major feature release with preset system, extraction history, frame preview, and batch extraction.

ul.li: Preset system to save, browse, and apply named extraction presets
Extraction history with one-click open folder and copy path
Frame preview screen with scrubber and set-as-start/end controls
Batch extraction across multiple time ranges in a single run
Live frame count and estimated output size display
Video metadata card showing duration, resolution, FPS, and codec
Drag and drop video files onto the app window
Settings persistence across sessions
Real-time time range validation with inline error messages
Close confirmation dialog when extraction is in progress

description.p: Update checker, new application icon, and CI/CD fixes.

ul.li: Added update checker
New FrameExtractor application icon for Windows and Android
Added RPM build support
Fixed AppImage launch failure
Fixed application crash on Android at startup

description.p: Style and theme switcher, keyboard shortcuts, and Linux AppImage fix.

ul.li: Classic and Liquid Glass (experimental) style switcher
Dark and Light theme switcher
Keyboard shortcuts: Space (Extract), Esc (Cancel), Ctrl+L (Log), Ctrl+S (Settings)
Log and Settings now appear as dialogs on desktop
Fixed Linux AppImage launch error caused by unexpanded variable in AppRun

description.p: Android extraction fixes and UI improvements.

ul.li: Fixed frame extraction on Android with Scoped Storage support
Fixed YouTube download error on Android external storage
Improved SAF URI resolution with fallback to writable app directory
Mouse cursor and text cursor improvements on interactive elements
Hint bar below Extract button explaining required selections
Clear button on video file and output folder rows
Color-coded log lines and log line count badge
Progress card background tinted by current phase

description.p: Initial release with local and YouTube extraction.

ul.li: Extract frames from local video files with start/end time control
Extract frames directly from YouTube URLs via yt-dlp
Adjustable FPS (1–60), format (PNG, JPG, WebP, BMP), quality, and scale
Custom filename prefix for extracted frames
Real-time log panel with copy-to-clipboard support
Live progress tracking with percentage, frame count, and ETA
Bundled ffmpeg and yt-dlp — no manual installation needed
Support for Windows, Linux, and Android
